newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Airtours cuts losses, sees sunny summer.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Airtours cuts losses, sees sunny summer.

text.p: British tour operator Airtours Plc on Wednesday reported a sharp cut in first-quarter losses and forecast a sunny outlook for summer bookings.

The company said its pre-tax loss narrowed by about 34 percent to 12.1 million pounds ($19.43 million) for the first quarter ended December 31, while turnover rose by 40 percent to 381.1 million pounds.
"It's been an extremely satisfactory first quarter," deputy chief executive Harry Coe told Reuters in an interview.
"I think to have reduced our losses is a not inconsiderable achievement. Demand in the marketplace is quite strong at the moment, and forward bookings also reflect that," he added.
Airtours normally has losses in the first half of its financial year and profits in the second half, reflecting European tourists' preference for summer holidays.

The company said summer bookings in Britain, which accounts for more than half of its business, were up 45 percent, while like-for-like bookings from its Scandinavian operations grew 20 percent compared to last year.
Like-for-like bookings in Canada were 8.0 percent higher during the winter, one of its busiest holiday seasons.
However, Airtours said passenger volumes for the year would be roughly in line with last year due to widely-expected capacity constraints.

"In reality, we will not end up at the end of the year with the sort of increases that are talked about because we haven't got that sort of increase in capacity available for sale," chairman David Crossland said.
"Hopefully, because we've booked more people earlier from brochures, we'll have a better mix of business and a better margin on that business," he added.
Advance brochure bookings are generally more lucrative for holiday operators than later sales, which may be offered at steep discounts.
Airtours said it had about 2.8 million passengers out of Britain last year, 1.4 million from Scandinavia and roughly 300,000 out of Canada.
Airtours' results and bright summer outlook prompted at least one brokerage to upgrade its profit forecast for the firm.
"The results were good. They were in line with forecasts," one analyst said.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett raised its estimates for Airtours' full-year pre-tax profits to 110 million pounds from 103 million and kept a buy rating on the stock, market sources said.
An ABN AMRO analyst declined to comment.
Airtours' shares slid 6.5 pence to 970.0 by 1140 GMT after rising on Tuesday amid speculation that U.S. tour operator Carnival Corp might raise its stake in the firm.
Airtours officials said they had made progress with Carnival on the companies' previously-announced plan to buy Italian cruise line Costa Crociere SpA, but they declined to comment on further deals.
Crossland reiterated that the company was on the lookout for strategic acquisitions.

"We have a strong balance sheet, very strong cash reserves, and we're interested in growing our business in other European countries and also in the large North American market," he said. ($1=.6227 Pound)
